transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Any time I have to get blood drawn, I go to great lengths to avoid it or sit there in sheer terror the whole time. It has become a major hurdle for me, and I just don't know what to do about it anymore.
When you have to get blood drawn, is the fear mainly about the needle itself, seeing blood, or both? Have you ever felt faint or actually passed out during or around these situations?

The fear is mostly about the needle going into my vein, which just feels incredibly dangerous to me now. About a year ago, I actually fainted during a routine blood draw and broke my wrist when I fell. Now, even just thinking about getting blood taken makes me feel light-headed, like I might pass out all over again.
Besides blood draws, do you get the same intense fear or faint feeling with other things like shots, seeing blood, or medical procedures? Or is it only when blood is drawn from your vein?

It is really just about having blood drawn from my vein because of that awful fall, not regular shots or other medical procedures. In fact, even seeing a picture of a blood draw on a clinic poster triggers my anxiety, and I only canceled my cataract surgery because it required those pre-operative labs.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a marked, cued, and avoidant fear focused specifically on venipuncture/blood draws, with immediate anxiety and vasovagal light-headedness/fainting triggered by direct exposure and even images. The fear is disproportionate, persistent since a traumatic fainting episode during blood draw, and causes clear functional impairment, consistent with specific phobia, blood-injection-injury type.
